brief.subject: Final 401(k) auto-enrollment rules land; SBA updates two programs
brief.headline: IRS Finalizes 401(k) and 403(b) Auto-Enrollment Rules; SBA Revises SBIC and Surety Bond Programs
brief.dek: Employers get final SECURE 2.0 auto-enrollment guidance, while SBA expands SBIC leverage and simplifies its surety bond guarantee program.
brief.lede: Treasury and the IRS have issued final regulations on SECURE 2.0's automatic enrollment requirement for 401(k) and 403(b) plans. Employers sponsoring these plans should review how the rules apply to them.

sections.heading: Auto-enrollment rules are now final
bullets: Treasury and the IRS issued final regulations implementing SECURE 2.0's automatic enrollment requirement for 401(k) and 403(b) plans.
Certain cash or deferred arrangements must be eligible automatic contribution arrangements that meet additional requirements, so plan design may need updating.
The rules affect employers maintaining these plans as well as participants and beneficiaries, making them relevant for payroll and benefits setup.

sections.heading: SBA raises SBIC leverage limits
bullets: An SBA interim final rule implements the Investing in All of America Act of 2025 for Small Business Investment Companies.
SBICs issuing standard debentures can access more leverage, at ratios of up to two-to-one against private capital.
More leverage for these funds could expand the investment capital available to small businesses.

sections.heading: Surety bond program gets streamlined
bullets: An SBA final rule reduces document submission and retention burdens for surety companies in the Surety Bond Guarantee program.
Less paperwork for sureties may ease bonding for small contractors who rely on SBA-backed bonds.
The rule also fixes conflicting provisions and revises outdated Preferred Surety admissions and Quarterly Contract Completion Report requirements.

sections.heading: Scholarship tax credit hearing moves to phone
bullets: The December 15, 2026 hearing on proposed rules for the federal scholarship tax credit will be held by telephone only.
The proposed rules cover the non-refundable credit for qualified contributions to scholarship granting organizations.
Regulators say they intend to allow scholarship funds to cover a broad range of K-12 educational needs.

brief.seo_description: Final IRS rules on 401(k) and 403(b) auto-enrollment, SBA SBIC leverage and surety bond changes, and a scholarship tax credit hearing update.

items.title: Rule: Surety Bond Guarantee Program: Streamlining and Modernizing
items.snippet: This final rule makes several changes to the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) Surety Bond Guarantee (SBG) program regulations. The rule reduces the burden on participating surety companies for submission and retention of documents. The rule also corrects conflicting provisions, as well as revising the obsolete Preferred Surety admissions requirements and the Quarterly Contract Completion Report.
